doc.title: Billy Bauer interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, March 22, 1998

title: The Herman rhythm section: Chubby Jackson and Davy Tough
summary: Chubby's shouting drove the section while Davy Tough was not flashy; Flip says Davy took his only solo on Bauer's tune.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Tell me about the rhythm section with Chubby and you and Davy Tough.
Yeah, and then we had a few piano players, but Ralph was the one that when I came there he was the piano player. That was a crazy business. It was, I guess a lot of it, just like that

shouting and everything, that was all Chubby Jackson. You know, “go ahead” and all that. And but the rhythm section with Davy Tough, I mean he just knew where, he wasn’t a flashy drummer. As a matter of fact I met Flip, well I guess at his birthday, but he told me that the only solo that Davy every took is on my tune, which was I think “Skyscraper” that I recorded with Flip Phillips. A big hit.
